_comment: The complete interface between the harness and whatever launches it. This file is the
ONLY thing the two sides share; they share no code at all.
That is deliberate. A shared Python package does not even guarantee agreement — a pip
install served a stale engine out of a Docker layer cache exactly once, which is how
the lesson was learned — whereas a versioned contract can be tested independently from
both sides. The harness asserts it honours this file; the loader asserts every spec it
It is also served live at GET /v1/contract, so a loader can validate against the
contract of the exact image it is about to launch rather than against a vendored copy

env._comment: Supplied BY the loader, consumed BY the harness. The harness computes none of these; it refuses to start rather than defaulting, because every default is a second definition of something the loader owns.

required_always.PODH_WORKSPACE: root of the mounted data view, e.g. /workspace
required_always.PODH_LOG_ROOT: directory for run output. The harness used to derive this as $PODH_WORKSPACE/runs, which meant the layout was defined here AND in the loader; the copies drifted three times in one day.

required_for_batch.PODH_JOB_ID: the job this pod owns. Assigned at creation, never discovered — workers that scan for work can race, and object storage cannot arbitrate.
required_for_batch.PODH_JOB_SPEC: absolute path to the job spec, written BEFORE the pod is created
required_for_batch.PODH_RUN_PREFIX: object-key prefix where this job publishes status, e.g. runs/<job_id>
required_for_batch.PODH_WRITE_PREFIXES: comma-separated object-key prefixes this job may write to. The harness refuses any write outside them. A harness that could write anywhere could overwrite corpus/raw/, the one thing here that cannot be regenerated.

optional.PODH_CODE_ROOT: path to the workload's code; prepended to PYTHONPATH. Absent means run the image's baked code, and the harness says which it used.
optional.PODH_API_TOKEN: bearer token for /v1. Absent disables the API.
optional.PODH_ENTRY: override the batch entry module (default pod_harness.execute_job)
optional.PODH_CONTROL_URL: control plane base URL. Absent: no /alive, /boot or /done is sent, and nothing else changes.
optional.PODH_CONTROL_TOKEN: pod-scoped token sent as X-Podh-Token on every control call. It speaks for this pod only.
optional.PODH_CONTROL_FINGERPRINT: SHA-256 of the control plane's DER certificate (openssl's colon form). Pins TLS; absent leaves default verification, under which a self-signed endpoint simply fails.
optional.PODH_CONTROL_JOB_ID: job id the scoped token is bound to; defaults to PODH_JOB_ID
optional.PODH_GPU_COUNT: GPUs the job asked for. >0: the GPU check runs and expects at least this many; 0: CPU pod, check skipped; unset (older launchers): checked only if nvidia-smi exists and lists a GPU.
optional.PODH_GPUCHECK_PYTHON: comma-separated interpreters to run the CUDA probe with; the first that imports torch is used. Default python3.
optional.PODH_GPUCHECK_TIMEOUT: CUDA probe timeout in seconds, default 120
optional.PODH_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SEC: beats stop once console output and job events have been still this long (default 1800), so a hung workload goes quiet. 0 disables the gate.
optional.PODH_HEARTBEAT_STOP_FILE: the flag that silences the heartbeat at done; default /tmp/podh-stop-heartbeat. Exists for tests.
optional.PODH_LOCAL_PORT: podh-boot's local API port on 127.0.0.1; default ephemeral
optional.PODH_LOCAL_TOKEN: token for the local API; default random. Exported to the app and workload.
optional.PODH_LOCAL_URL: set BY podh-boot for the app stage, the workload and app.serve: the local API (POST /busy, GET /state, POST /done). podh-report busy|idle|done use it.
optional.PODH_BOOT_SPEC: podh-boot: read the boot spec from this JSON file instead of GET /v1/pod/spec
optional.PODH_BOOT_DIR: podh-boot's state, logs and binaries; default $PODH_WORKSPACE/.podh-boot (PODH_WORKSPACE default /workspace), else ~/.podh-boot
optional.PODH_BOOT_EXIT: 1 = podh-boot exits with the rc when the pod's work ends (as --exit-on-fail) instead of idling
optional.PODH_MODELS_ROOT: where models land; ComfyUI's model folders point here. Default $PODH_WORKSPACE/models. Exported to the app and workload.
optional.PODH_WORKLOAD_ENV: KEY=value file the binaries stage and the app stage write, loaded (with $VAR expansion) into the workload and app.serve. Default <boot dir>/workload.env. Exported.
optional.PODH_COMFY_ROOT: the ComfyUI dir; default the first of /opt/ComfyUI, /workspace/runpod-slim/ComfyUI, /workspace/ComfyUI with main.py. Exported.
optional.PODH_COMFY_PY: the workload's python (addons install into it, probes run with it); default the ComfyUI venv, else python3. Exported.
optional.PODH_ADDONS_ROOT: where addons are cloned; default $PODH_COMFY_ROOT/custom_nodes, else <boot dir>/addons
optional.PODH_BAKED_ROOT: set by images built for podh-boot: what the image installed at build time. bin/<name>-<sha12>/ (a pinned binary with its marker) is used instead of downloading the same sha256; addons.json {addons: {name: {commit, dir}}} marks checkouts whose requirements.txt the build installed, so a job pinning the same commit skips the clone and requirements.txt (pip extras, links and probes still run). Unset: nothing is baked.
optional.PODH_APP_DIR: same as PODH_APP_ROOT (kept as an alias)
optional.PODH_IMAGE_DIGEST: the image's digest, if the image knows it; part of every kit's key
optional.PODH_KIT_FORMAT: zst | gz for kits this pod publishes; default zst when the zstd binary exists
optional.PODH_NO_ARIA2: 1 = never use aria2c for downloads, even when present
optional.PODH_PIP_TIMEOUT: seconds per addon pip install, default 1200
optional.PODH_APP_ROOT: set BY podh-boot: where app.fetch is unpacked (boot.app.dir, else /opt/app); {app} in app.run/app.serve argv; their cwd. PODH_APP_DIR is the same path.

provider_supplied.RUNPOD_POD_ID: set by RunPod; used only for labelling, never for logic

spec._comment: Written by the loader, read by the harness. `params` is opaque to both — only the workload interprets it. Everything else is framework surface the harness acts on.

idempotency_key.description: optional, unique. A re-POST returns the existing job rather than starting a second pod-hour — agents retry on timeout, and this makes that safe.

root.description: immutable code/<workload>/<rev>/, or code/<workload>/dev/ for iteration

stages_from.description: module:attribute naming the workload's stage registry

runner.description: how to provision. The harness ignores this entirely — it is the loader talking to itself, carried in the spec so a job record is self-describing.

from.description: auto | <stage name> | never. `auto` re-runs verify_outputs() per completed stage and restarts at the first that does not verify. Never marker-driven: a .DONE marker once survived a wiped volume and reported 'done: 24' over no outputs.

events._comment: Written by the harness, read by the loader. Append-only JSON lines plus an atomically-replaced status.json snapshot.

files.$PODH_LOG_ROOT/$PODH_JOB_ID/status.json: snapshot, atomic replace. Carries `stages` (last-writer: where is this job now) and, for a chunked run, `chunks` = {chunk: {stage: outcome}} (which units of work reached which stage). Two structures because they answer two questions and both are asked.
files.$PODH_RUN_PREFIX/status.json: the same snapshot in object storage, so status survives the pod

seq.description: monotonic per job. A client resumes from where it stopped on any transport.

chunk.description: The unit of work a chunk-scoped stage ran under; empty or absent for a job-scoped stage. Part of the event's IDENTITY, not a detail: `align` on one chunk and `align` on another are two executions with two outcomes, and without this they are the same event twice.

invariants: `state` carries StageResult.status verbatim. Collapsing `unverified` into `ok` would make status report green for exactly the bug class the verification layer exists to catch: three separate bugs where a stage reported success and produced nothing.
`seq` never decreases and never repeats within a job.
A terminal job answers a long-poll immediately rather than waiting out the timeout.

A chunked run records every (chunk, stage) outcome under `chunks`. `stages` remains last-writer and is not redefined: seven stages over three chunks write seven keys there, and the fourteen discarded outcomes include the failure that stopped the run.
`chunk` is additive to contract_version 1. A reader that ignores it sees exactly what it saw before, which is why the version does not bump.

api._comment: Identical on a pod and on a control plane, so a client written against one works against the other. That is what lets compute move to serverless or another vendor without touching callers.
api.auth: Bearer token or X-Podh-Token header; /v1/health is unauthenticated

endpoints.note: discovery: endpoints, stage vocabulary, spec schema
this file, as served by the running harness

invariants: No unbounded responses: every payload is capped and reports total_bytes/truncated.
dry_run costs nothing and starts no stage.
Submit is idempotent when idempotency_key is supplied.
Errors carry a `hint` naming the fix.

responses._comment: Response shapes a loader depends on. Added because my own polling scripts read `state` twice in one day when the job endpoint returns `job_state` — the poll silently reported None while the job had genuinely failed. An endpoint list is not enough; the keys are part of the interface.

properties.job_state: queued | running | done | failed | cancelled — NOT `state`
properties.seq: integer, cursor into the event stream
properties.stages: object keyed by stage name; each has state, index, seconds, verification

_comment: Calls the POD makes TO the control plane — the reverse direction of `api`.
Every one is best-effort: the control plane polls the provider and is the authority, so a lost
call costs money, never correctness. Optional fields were added after the first servers shipped;
a server that answers 400/422 to a key it does not know is sent the request again without them.
Extra keys beyond these lists may be present and must be ignored, not rejected.
control_plane.auth: X-Podh-Token: $PODH_CONTROL_TOKEN; TLS pinned to $PODH_CONTROL_FINGERPRINT when set, checked after the handshake and before the request is written

calls.note: sent every PODH_HEARTBEAT_SEC only while the pod produces output; quiet means stuck or finished. busy/detail: is the app's work running now (podh-boot sends them; the idle clock runs only while busy is false). Reply {extend_until, drain, park, models_rev}; extra reply keys are ignored.
one line per boot step. stage "ready" means the workload is up. A server without this route answers 404 and the pod carries on.
terminate me. rc is how it ended; reason/stage say why and where, for a failure. log_tail: the end of the workload's log (≤1 KB, newlines kept) on a failure.

stages._comment: stage values podh-init and podh-boot send. A sidecar workload may send its own.

exit_codes.7: the GPU is unusable (podh-gpucheck; podh-init reports it as done rc 7, stage gpu_check)

_comment: The /v1/pod/* routes: what a booting pod ASKS the control plane for. Same token and pin as `calls`.
No bytes pass through the control plane: it answers with presigned URLs, and those URLs are fetched WITHOUT the pod token.
`client` names the module that makes the call; assert_contract.py checks the path appears there.

reply.401/403/404: fatal at stage spec; other answers are retried for boot.limits.spec (default 300 s)

calls.note: {boot, policy, ...} or a bare boot object. Keys podh-boot reads under boot: gpu_check, binaries, models, addons, app, workload, limits.

reply.404: an older server: the app gets the container env

calls.note: every boot, resumed or not: the CURRENT job's app env. Exported to app.run and app.serve over the container env; job_id becomes PODH_JOB_ID.

200: files[]: path, url, sha256?, size?, boot?

calls.note: presigned GETs, fetched WITHOUT the pod token. Asked again when a link is refused (401/403) and on a higher models_rev. boot:false files never fail the boot; they are fetched after ready.
{"models": {path: "fetching" | "present" | {"state": "failed", "error"}}}, one path per call, best effort
items per APP-API §2 'Addon item schema'; validated again on the pod
after gpu_check (vram_gb number, cuda, driver, gpu = first card's name) and again after the NVENC probe (nvenc bool). Best effort; any answer is ignored.

reply.404: no kit for this key and these facts yet

calls.note: name ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$. The archive is verified against sha256 before it is unpacked; tar.zst or tar.gz, detected by magic bytes.

reply.409: already published, or another pod holds the claim; the caller does not publish

calls.note: claim the build and get a presigned PUT for the archive

reply.other: the kit is not published; not fatal to a boot

local_api._comment: Served by podh-boot on 127.0.0.1 for the app's worker. Auth: X-Podh-Token: $PODH_LOCAL_TOKEN (or Authorization: Bearer). /health needs none.

routes.note: rides on the next /alive (sent within ~2 s of a flip)

drain/park/extend_until/window_until/models_rev are the last /alive reply's (window_until: end of the paid keep-warm/idle window, when the control plane sends it); models is {path: present|fetching|failed}
the only exit: reported to the control plane, and podh-boot stops what it supervises
stop and start the workload; 200 once it answers again (within up_timeout_s); 409 no workload / pod ended; 503 {error, log_tail} when it does not come back. Does not count as a crash.

fetch models now, mid-life (a held task's): files [{path, url, sha256?, size?}] carry their links, bare paths are looked up in a fresh GET /v1/pod/models. 202 at once; each path's state then shows in /state models. 422 bad path, 503 no models machinery.

boot._comment: podh-boot: the job's boot spec as ordered, time-limited stages. APP-API §4.
boot.resume: binaries, models, addons and app are skipped when the disk already has them (per sha / commit / definition); gpu_check always runs; --fresh ignores the disk
binary_item: env?  ({bin} and {bindir} = the install dir; $VAR expanded against the env)
bin_names?  (absent: every executable in the shallowest bin/ holding one named like the binary)

endings.stage failure: done(rc, reason, stage, log_tail), then idle (exit with --exit-on-fail)
endings.workload: fatal CUDA string → rc 7 stage gpu_check; scan_log_for hit, or a second crash → stage workload
endings.app.serve: exit 0 → done(0), except under drain/park (the pod idles); a second crash → stage app_serve; drain/park → SIGTERM, serve_grace_s, SIGKILL, and the pod stays up

exit_codes.7: GPU unusable (gpu_check, or a fatal CUDA string in the workload log)
exit_codes.other: the failing step's own rc where it has one, else 1

boot.app_env: GET /v1/pod/env, over the container env, for app.run and app.serve

exports._also: PODH_MODELS_ROOT, PODH_WORKLOAD_ENV, PODH_BOOT_DIR, PODH_COMFY_ROOT, PODH_COMFY_PY, PODH_APP_ROOT, PODH_LOCAL_URL, PODH_LOCAL_TOKEN
